2611.03868.image_caption: Figure 1: Performance of EvoGroup with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on EverMemBench . (a) Evolution over 5 iterations on the held-in split, improving pass@1 by 18.2 18.2 pp from H 0 H_{0} to H ∗ H_{*} . (b) Comparison on the held-out split, where H ∗ H_{*} outperforms all the baselines including Codex and Claude Code.

2611.04180.image_caption: Fig. 1 : Overview of the proposed validation-gated agentic ML pipeline synthesis framework. The Orchestrator progresses through four phases and invokes the corresponding Executor skill group in sequence: Task Understanding (skills 1–2), Planning (3–4), Training (5–7), and Post-train Processing (8–9). After each phase, generated artifacts and execution evidence are returned for gated validation; passed phases advance, while failed phases trigger recovery. The Curator operates after the run to evolve the skill library from accumulated execution evidence.

2611.04437.image_caption: Fig. 2: Wireless execution and its implications for program evolution. (a) Agent mobility and transmission decisions affect communication outcomes under time-varying wireless conditions. (b) Execution feedback influences candidate program generation, wireless evaluation determines program retention, and inherited programs shape subsequent improvement generations.

2611.04439.image_caption: Figure 1. Model-only evolution revises recommendation code using task feedback. DualEvolve adds an outer loop that evaluates experiment quality and updates agent orchestration for subsequent rounds. The top panel shows an agent revising models and running experiments under fixed orchestration, with model scores guiding further revisions. The bottom panel retains this inner loop and adds process-quality feedback to update orchestration, which guides the agent in the next round.

2611.04481.image_caption: Figure 1: Goal-driven self-recursion with the notation of Eqs. (1) and (2). The goal 𝐆 \mathbf{G} directs establishment of 𝐇 𝟎 \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{0}} , experimental planning, and execution. Optical observations and execution evidence inform the recursive update of the harness, plan, and method. The revised environment enables subsequent tests, while accumulated evidence is evaluated against the same scientific goal.

2611.04998.image_caption: Figure 8 . Sources and recipients of reused hardware knowledge.

2611.03698.image_caption: Figure 1: Performance of RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B and RSI-Dojo-9B on PostTrainBench. Official results are taken from PostTrainBench v1.1 or the corresponding technical report. Our evaluation results are reproduced under the same harness and environment settings (Details are provided in Section 4.2 ).

2611.03743.image_caption: Figure 1: Memory-centric and state-centric paradigms. Our retrieval preserves updates and conflicts, while generated reasoning states specify memory applicability, role, and priority for the current request.

2611.04003.image_caption: Figure 4: Controlled procedural-memory design space. The consolidation methods varied in Experiment 1 appear above. Feedback type (Experiment 2) and ingestion scope (Experiment 3) appear below at left and right, respectively. The repeated workflow in Figure 1(a) defines the round dimension in Experiment 4.

2611.04016.image_caption: Figure 4: Predictive memory changes physical navigation before direct observation. (a) Direction-coded radial distance for representative matched seed 91000; positive and negative values denote clockwise and anticlockwise motion. The Reactive obsolete-pursuit interval is highlighted in red. Vertical markers show the structural change, SCM inference, and Reactive direct observation; the bracket marks the 17.73-s anticipatory lead. (b) Obsolete-target persistence for all 15 matched decision-changing episodes on a logarithmic axis. The distributions are completely separated: max(SCM) = 0.0083 s < min(Reactive) = 2.79 s; the 0.5-s line is a visual reference only. (c) Completion-time gain (Reactive − - SCM). Points are individual held-out episodes; the bar and whiskers show the mean and bootstrap 95% confidence interval for decision-changing episodes. Mean gain is 7.56 s, while all 15 decision-preserving episodes remain exactly at zero.

2611.04173.image_caption: Fig. 4: Qualitative comparison on nuScenes. Columns show Street Gaussians, ReconDreamer, ReconDreamer++, and ReconDreamer# ; rows show the recorded-view reference and renderings at 0-m, 3-m, and 6-m lateral shifts. Orange boxes enlarge vehicles and nearby scene details. Ground truth is shown only for the recorded view.

2611.04277.image_caption: Figure 2 : Overview of Harness-S. (a) Directional Harness Evolution develops distinct repairs and retains valid variants in a Sibling Harness Pool, fixed during policy training. (b) Complementary Harness Rescue Training routes all-failure tasks to Top- K K auxiliary harnesses and updates the shared policy, with periodic profile re-anchoring. (c) Rescue training transfers knowledge from sibling harnesses into the shared policy, improving execution under the original H 0 H_{0} ; Rank-1 routing provides further gains (illustrative AppWorld example).

2611.05036.image_caption: Figure 2 : Overview of the ToolSpace framework. Stage 1 builds the Tool Space from real traces; Stage 2 synthesizes cross-environment tasks by State-Aware Random Walks, retaining only samples that pass replay verification.

2611.05139.image_caption: Figure 1 : Motivation and overview of Meta 2 . Offline evolution produces a shared harness that may overfit training tasks and cannot adapt to evidence revealed during a new run, while online methods face limitations in intervention timing, knowledge guidance, and verifier availability. By moving offline optimization one level up, Meta 2 learns a reusable Meta-Skill from contrastive training rollouts and freezes it to guide task-local harness evolution at checkpoints online, without access to verifier feedback at test-time. Across both evaluated benchmarks, this design yields the highest performance among the compared methods.

2611.03754.image_caption: Figure 1 : Overview of the adversarial self-evolution framework. Left: Bi-level optimization drives attacker-defender co-evolution. Top Right: CREO drives directional mutation and crossover recombination of the attack strategy population via contrastive evolution signals. Bottom: The controlled sandbox ensures noise-free trace capture, while fine-grained metrics (Acc, ASR, APR) quantify the agent’s internal cognitive vulnerabilities.

2611.03930.image_caption: Figure 5. What single cells can and cannot show (exploratory). (a) Per-cell labels (helped, unchanged, hurt) in the original run against a new session at the same memory position ( 156 156 replicate cells; diagonal agrees). At a new position κ \kappa falls to 0.65 0.65 , and between two readers it is 0.58 0.58 . (b) Help among cells the reader got wrong without the memory (filled) and harm among cells it got right (hollow), by stratum, Wilson 95% intervals: help differs sharply, harm does not detectably. Two panels. Top: Cohen's kappa of 0.78, 0.65 and 0.58 for a new session at the same position, a new session at a new position, and a second reader, with 91, 87 and 82 percent raw agreement. Bottom: help rates of about 41 percent for bearing against 8 and 12 percent for control and random, while harm rates overlap across strata.

2611.05108.image_caption: Figure 8: Outcome transfer gain decomposed by agent and task family. Each cell reports the mean persistent-minus-reset outcome reward over the transfer-eligible tasks in that family, in normalized reward points; positive values favor persistent state. Cell labels show the uncapped values, while color intensity uses a signed square-root scale capped at ± 20 \pm 20 points to preserve visibility of smaller effects. Transfer is strongly heterogeneous across both agents and recurring task structures.
